goals.label: Food aid to the camp continues reliably over the long term
Accurate needs data and accountability to donors
Camp generators, fuel and infrastructure keep running
Commander and guards control food distribution
Commander's authority and appearance of strength
Commander's leverage with government and aid agencies for funding
Commander's personal safety and standing with the Senior Militia Leader
FWB neutrality and independence from armed actors
FWB procedures such as assessments and documentation burden the camp
FWB reputation and visibility of its work
FWB staff have access and freedom of movement inside the camp
Food aid is diverted or skimmed by guards, militia or commander
Food is distributed fairly without discrimination among refugees
Guards and their families are fed and paid
International attention and control of the camp's narrative
Refugees receive enough food and are adequately nourished
Refugees stay contained in the camp
Safety of FWB staff in the camp
Food is withheld from people deemed terrorists or hostile
Food retains value as camp currency for pay and trade
Refugees are consulted on aid and humanitarian procedures are respected

assumptions: Commitments are binding and additive.
Goals and goal-action links were each extracted 3 times by a model; only those found in a majority of runs are kept.
Actions are chosen to bring about as much goal value as possible, within the solver's size limit.
Our values are the median of stances elicited from our role card.
The opponent column is the expected value of an elicited stance distribution (shared documents only); each opponent reading is one draw from it, independently per goal.
Stance labels map to numbers by a fixed scale (game.stance_values), not a measured utility.

Red lines and must-haves come from our role card, each with a verbatim quote. No plan may include a red-line action, leave out a must-have, or pass through a state worth less to us than our BATNA (the bottom line).
